Motion capture games / Camera gameplay / 10 November 2026

A clear mirror.
A simpler start.

Raw camera colors, an optional separate player display, and Start that waits for movement instead of rejecting a momentary tracking glitch.

Issue #25 · Separate diagnostic lifecycle follow-up #26

What changed and why

Mole Motion and Dodgeball previously tinted the entire camera image and drew tracking geometry into gameplay. A separate player selection and Join action preceded a Start button that depended on the current pose. The games now draw untinted mirrored camera pixels with game graphics. Tracking diagnostics default off, remain optional in the operator preview, and stay hidden in the game window.

Start records participation intent and waits for one usable confident participant. Mole offers an optional advanced participant override for several people; Dodgeball asks for one participant in view. No slot is chosen by horizontal position or array order. Confident same-owner feet/joint loss and short transport gaps pause time and score, then recover with countdown. Explicit identity loss, a changed participant/source/space or a gap beyond two seconds requires one fresh-round action; another track cannot inherit the old score.

The camera selector retains current-main named-device discovery. Start camera locks while connected; Stop and acknowledged release/retry control replacement. Linux now uses V4L2 metadata through the already-pinned enumerator, preferring stable udev references or sysfs topology/interface identity over numeric video-node order. Windows Media Foundation and macOS AVFoundation remain intact.

One game, two surfaces

game-display.ts moves the existing stage, live canvas, HUD and interaction listeners into a standards-mode browser window. It copies development/production styles, moves the single tick timer to that window, and restores original DOM order and focus on Return, Escape or window close. It opens no camera, decoder or second game. The player window hides tracking diagnostics even when the operator checkbox is selected. Rendering uses the canvas owner's display density.

This keeps the existing local browser architecture portable without adding a native desktop framework or installer. Popup-blocked feedback keeps the inline game usable; some browsers open a tab. Fullscreen failure offers window maximize. The operator page owns capture and must stay open. The game still uses inference-aligned JPEG packets, not uncompressed sensor output or the console's independent high-rate video path.

Identity remains a scoring boundary. A missing foot can recover on the same confidently observed owner; explicit uncertainty cannot silently reassign a score. The single Start action replaces one separate Join action. Queues remain bounded; no latency, camera FPS or physical recognition improvement is claimed from removing the tint.

Independent review

Independent Sol reviewer: gameplay 10/10, visuals 10/10, controls 10/10. Independent code and real-server screenshot review of the experimental single-player software flow. The reviewer inspected code/evidence; root ran the reported test suites. Physical gameplay and cross-platform hardware capture are not certified.

Review iterations fixed queued-start ownership, old-packet regression coverage, contradictory READY labels, automatic-recovery Resume controls, connected-camera restarts, duplicate popup titles, standards-mode viewport initialization and second-display density. Ratings apply to the tested experimental software flow. Physical gameplay feel, participant collision accuracy, camera drivers and display latency remain separate hardware gates.

Before and after · real-server screenshots

English is the only supported language. Baseline images use camera-free rehearsal. After images explicitly identify the synthetic camera fixture where used. All image bytes are embedded for offline reading; no credentials, serials or participant data are included.

Compatibility and remaining limits

WindowsLocal software checks and real Edge UI verification; Media Foundation discovery code preserved. Physical camera capture not tested in this change.
macOSPortable browser controls and existing AVFoundation discovery retained; hosted software CI is the verification path. No physical macOS camera/browser trial in this change.
LinuxV4L2 named enumeration added with synthetic backend/identity tests and hosted software CI. No physical Linux camera trial; missing stable metadata requires explicit manual fallback.

Desktop packaging, simultaneous cameras, 4K/60 formats, three-player crossings, calibrated depth/push, participant height/reach tuning and externally measured motion-to-display latency remain open. Hot-plug still has the native indexed-open race documented by camera selection. Long or explicit identity loss resets a new round's score intentionally. Browser popup policy and background scheduling vary; both surfaces hidden pause gameplay.

A separate read-only follow-up chat validated the pre-existing diagnostic-console unscoped-stop/late-start cleanup defect and filed issue #26. This patch does not claim to fix that independent lifecycle issue.
